cells.tense: You are standing in a clearing you made, and you know it is yours.
cells.ask: Name one resource you could hand on today and pass it, plainly, without managing what happens to it after.
cells.core:
You are handing on what you have, at a measure you picked. The strength is real. It moves between you and the people around you, and it moves because you move it. Nothing here is forced or performed. You are giving at a rate you chose, into an ending you have already accepted. Someone nearby is steadier because of what you passed them, and you did not make it a debt.

The clearing is open, and what you hand on goes into it without bargaining. For the next stretch, keep it deliberate: choose what flows and let it leave your hands. What was over has stopped being fed. That is why the ground is steady enough to stand on, and why what you give out lands where it is meant to.
cells.sheetLine: You are giving what is yours to give, into a clearing you chose.
cells.place: the clearing where what was ends for what comes next

cells.tense: You are pushing support toward a future nobody has reached yet.
cells.ask: Let one person wait a day before you carry the next thing for them, and hold the answer that comes back.
cells.core:
You are supplying a future that has not happened. Someone may need this, so you have it ready — and the readiness has become a kind of steering. You are holding up a clearing you cannot open on your own, and pushing makes the help arrive early and heavy.

The strength is real. What has tipped is the timing: you are pouring into a place that has not emptied. Holding without forcing is the other side of this, and it is available. Try letting the next need come to you before you answer it. The clearing will keep. Nobody has to be carried across it in advance.
cells.sheetLine: You are carrying weight for a future nobody asked you to brace.
cells.place: the clearing where what was ends for what comes next

cells.tense: You were at a door that has already closed, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Pick one thing already finished and tell one person you are done with it, without reopening the decision.
cells.core:
The clearing is here. The support is not. Something ended, and you did not step through — your strength stayed on the near side, where the old arrangement was. People around you set things down and waited to set them down with you. What stopped is not the ability to give. It is the release that lets giving be finished.

What is missing is letting something be over. Not failed, not taken from you — completed. Name one finished thing and leave it finished. Say it to another person, and let the saying stand. The clearing is not empty because it is unfinished. It is empty because what was there has ended.
cells.sheetLine: The ending happened. You are still handing things to the side that is over.
cells.place: the clearing where what was ends for what comes next

cells.tense: You are holding up more than you say, and you call it just how things are.
cells.ask: Say that this is yours, out loud, about one arrangement you have been holding up as if it were unanimous.
cells.core:
You are already the one holding this up, and no one is named in the story you tell about it. Support moves through you — decisions, reliability, the shape of the day — and you describe it as the work, the situation, the people. The arranging is running. Nobody has said it is yours.

That does not have to become a speech. It is one sentence in your own mouth that names the doing and the choosing. Say that once, and what you do stops looking automatic. The clearing gets easier to stand in when the standing is claimed. Then what you give comes from something that is actually yours.
cells.sheetLine: You are holding it up. You have not said so.
